We are Industrial Engineering students from Universidad Distrital in Bogotá, Colombia, passionate about astronomy, space exploration, and technology. We enjoy combining optimization, engineering, and creativity to develop innovative solutions. We promote scientific curiosity and demonstrate how engineering can support smarter decisions and resource management beyond Earth.

What we bring: Mathematical optimization, integer programming, and geospatial analysis

details:
ASTROKEEPERS: BEYOND EARTH

Guardians of Life Beyond Our World

ASTROKEEPERS: BEYOND EARTH is an educational and interactive video game designed to introduce players to the complexities of resource allocation and decision-making in space exploration missions. Through immersive scenarios inspired by lunar and Martian exploration, players assume the role of mission managers, responsible for operating a scientific outpost, optimizing limited resources, and ensuring the safety, health, and well-being of the crew.

The game provides an interactive environment in which players can explore and evaluate strategic decisions involving oxygen generation, habitat thermal regulation, rover deployment, communication systems, scientific and medical data transmission, and agricultural production to meet the crew’s nutritional requirements. Each decision directly influences mission performance, resource availability, operational feasibility, crew welfare, and scientific productivity.

Following the execution of a mission plan, the system evaluates the selected configuration against the mathematical model, verifies compliance with all operational constraints, and assesses its performance relative to the optimal solution. When a proposed configuration is infeasible, the system identifies the violated constraints, providing feedback that enables players to revise their decisions, test alternative strategies, and improve their understanding of the optimization process.

Multiobjective Optimization Model


A mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated to support decision-making for a manned mission to Mars, in the Jezero Crater. Three criteria are considered: energy consumption, crew health, and scientific research. First, the individual optimum for each criterion is calculated. Then, an overall solution is obtained through a weighted sum of the achievement percentages. This same mathematical formulation is also applied to model a lunar mission, where the underlying structure remains identical and only specific mission parameters—such as the number of astronauts—are modified.

In summary, ASTROKEEPERS is powered by a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model designed to manage resource allocation and operational decisions for space missions. The framework utilizes binary, integer, and continuous variables to balance three core performance criteria—crew health, energy consumption, and scientific research—through a weighted multi-criteria objective function that handles resource trade-offs. Bounded by strict operational constraints such as energy budgets, communication systems, and agricultural requirements, the model identifies mathematically feasible configurations to optimize overall mission performance.

Learning Through Decision-Making

The educational value of ASTROKEEPERS lies in its ability to translate a complex mathematical and engineering problem into an interactive, experience-based learning environment. Instead of passively observing equations or theoretical optimization results, players actively manipulate decision variables, execute different scenarios, and examine the operational consequences of their choices.

This experiential approach supports the understanding of fundamental concepts such as mathematical optimization, linear programming, constraint satisfaction, resource allocation, operational efficiency, and strategic decision-making. Furthermore, it promotes critical thinking and analytical reasoning by challenging players to evaluate competing priorities, identify resource limitations, interpret model feedback, and develop alternative strategies to improve mission outcomes.

Ultimately, the project seeks to foster interest in space exploration, engineering, mathematics, and STEM disciplines by demonstrating how mathematical modeling and computational optimization can be applied to address complex operational challenges and support evidence-based decision-making in real-world contexts.

A Different Approach to Learning Resource Management

ASTROKEEPERS introduces an innovative educational approach to resource management by integrating space exploration, interactive gameplay, and mathematical optimization into a unified learning experience. Rather than positioning users as passive observers of computational results, the project places them at the center of the decision-making process, allowing them to actively construct, evaluate, and refine mission strategies.

Its primary purpose is to make complex optimization concepts accessible through experimentation. Players are encouraged to test different configurations, identify infeasible decisions, analyze system feedback, and explore alternative solutions. This iterative process demonstrates that every operational decision has consequences and that effective resource management requires balancing competing objectives within clearly defined constraints.

Through this integration of mathematical modeling, computational technologies, and interactive learning, ASTROKEEPERS demonstrates how optimization can move beyond theoretical applications and become a practical tool for understanding complex systems, evaluating alternatives, and making informed decisions.

Technological Development



The ASTROKEEPERS prototype is implemented as a web-based application using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. SVG and Canvas technologies support the development of interactive visual environments, animations, and dynamic graphical elements. The reference mathematical model was developed in Python, leveraging NumPy and SciPy for numerical computation and optimization. The web-based implementation incorporates an optimization engine that evaluates player decisions and assesses mission configurations directly within the gameplay environment.

Additional features include a bilingual interface (English and Spanish) and a dedicated Science and Model Center, where users can explore the model’s parameters, decision variables, mathematical formulation, methodological foundations, and supporting references.

Future Implementation: Adaptable Parameters and Terrestrial Simulation


A future development of ASTROKEEPERS could expand its application beyond space exploration through the implementation of customizable parameter sets. This would allow users to adapt the mathematical model to different environmental conditions and resource availability.

For example, a future version could include a scenario inspired by the Tatacoa Desert in Colombia, using location-specific parameters to simulate the operation of a research station or habitat in this environment. Users could modify resource availability and environmental conditions to test different strategies, compare alternatives, and observe the consequences of their decisions.

This expansion would transform ASTROKEEPERS into a more versatile simulation and learning tool, applicable not only to space missions but also to terrestrial environments where resource management and decision-making are essential.
